matchups.recap: Kyle beat Brad 143.26-117.00, and Brad managed to make it worse by leaving Jaxson Dart's 26.6 points on the bench while Dak Prescott gave him 14.4 in the starting spot. Even with that gift of 12.2 points, Brad still loses by 14, so the lineup error was just the garnish on a Week 1 face-plant. Zay Flowers (26.0) and DJ Moore (21.0) both smashed their projections, and Brad still got hammered, mostly thanks to a Texans D/ST that scored -4.0. A team named "Free Josh Jacobs" also has Josh Jacobs sitting on its own bench for 0 points, which is the most Brad thing in the data. Kyle gets the win and the Kenneth Walker III (34.1) and Amon-Ra St. Brown (28.7) fireworks, but he also started Cameron Dicker for 2.0 points and Rome Odunze for 7.2 while Mike Evans (16.9) and Stefon Diggs (15.5) sat on his bench, so he won in spite of himself.

Josh beat Brett 109.86 to 89.16, and he did it with Ja'Marr Chase putting up 3.2 points, Jaylen Waddle 1.2, and Brandon Aubrey 2.0, while Kyle Monangai (20.4) and Deebo Samuel Sr. (18.0) sat on his bench watching. Trey McBride's 24.5 bailed Josh out, because that is a team with 38.4 points benched that still won by 20. Brett still managed to lose, posting the lowest score of the week and starting Colston Loveland, who scored a perfect zero, while Kenyon Sadiq dropped 11.4 on the bench at the same position. Brett also started Rico Dowdle (4.1) over Matthew Golden (15.5), and fixing just those two moves gets him to 111.96 and the win. Josh, enjoy the W, but your lineup tried its best to give it away, and Brett's lineup was somehow worse.

Reis beat Brandon 160.66 to 117.02, and Josh Allen's 35.66 points (against a 19.32 projection) did most of the work while Brandon watched from 43 points back. Brandon's Bobby Light had Cam Little's 12 kicker points outscoring Rashee Rice, a Chargers D/ST that put up a perfect zero, and Tre Tucker's 4.7 points in the flex while Caleb Douglas dropped 14.4 on the bench. Even the Douglas fix only gets Brandon to about 127, so he was never winning this one anyway. Reis wins, but he gets no credit for the lineup: Jalen Coker scored 33.8 on his bench while Courtland Sutton put up 3.1 in the flex spot, which is a 30-point swing he left sitting there. Reis won by 43 points and still managed to waste a 191-point week, and Brandon should be furious that Reis beat him while doing it that badly.

Tyler beat Noah 157.46 to 138.46, and he did it with Caleb Williams dropping 37.26 against a 16.39 projection, so congrats on a win built on a quarterback nobody should trust. Kyle Pitts put up a flat 0 at tight end and Terry McLaurin chipped in 3.4, yet Tyler still won by 19 because Derrick Henry (35.3) and Ashton Jeanty (32.7) did all the work. Tyler also left Chuba Hubbard's 23.7 on the bench while Omarion Hampton started and gave him 8.3, which is a 15-point gift to Noah that Noah couldn't even cash. Noah got huge games from Justin Jefferson (31.2) and David Montgomery (28.9), then wasted them on Drake London's 5.5 in the flex, Jake Ferguson's 2.6 at tight end, and a Broncos D/ST that scraped together 2.0. Puka Nacua managed 12.4 against a 21.05 projection, so Noah's lineup was a couple of stars with a pile of dead weight, and that's why he's 0-1.

Keith beat Cody 165.60 to 142.30, and the highest score of the week came from a manager who started a 1-point Rams defense, a 4.1-point Harold Fannin Jr. and a 5.6-point A.J. Brown, which tells you the scoreboard was just being nice to him. D'Andre Swift went for 32.40 from a flex spot where he was projected for 12.31, so Keith's "strategy" this week was a Taylor Swift pun and a prayer. Still, Cody handed over the win himself by parking Christian Watson's 32.70 on the bench while Tee Higgins sat in the lineup for 8.90, a swap that flips the game all by itself. Cody also left Isaiah Likely's 27.80 on the pine and started a 4.10 from Matthew Stafford and a 1-point kicker in Harrison Mevis, so the roster looked like it was built by someone who'd never watched a football game. Keith gets the W, but it was a gift-wrapped, no-receipt win, and the lineup crimes belong to Cody.

Josh beat Kyle 134.84 to 128.78, and he got there with a kicker: Brandon Aubrey dropped 17.0 and outscored Jayden Daniels (14.74), which is not how a "QB1" is supposed to work. Kyle lost by 6.06 points while Stefon Diggs sat on his bench for 21.7, and Malik Nabers cost him the game in the lineup with a 1.1 that rounds to "didn't show up." Amon-Ra St. Brown went off for 35.2 and Kyle still found a way to lose, which takes real commitment, especially with Cameron Dicker adding a 1.0 at kicker and Romeo Doubs (12.6) watching Rome Odunze (7.3) from the bench. Josh, don't get cute: Ja'Marr Chase's 26.5 carried you, and you started Rhamondre Stevenson (3.6) and Jameson Williams (5.3) while Blake Corum (10.2) and Xavier Worthy (13.5) sat on your bench. Congrats on the W, but you won by accident and Kyle lost on purpose.

Reis dropped 167.62 on Brad's 113.66, a 53.96-point beating, and it was the highest score of the week, powered by Josh Allen's 40.82 (on a 22.65 projection) and Davante Adams' 39.5 as Reis stumbled into the box score of the year. Reis even left Travis Kelce's 25.1 on the bench while Dallas Goedert coughed up 1.4 at tight end, so the blowout could have been even more obscene. Brad got a 29.76 from Dak Prescott and 22.6 from Christian McCaffrey and still lost by more than 50, which takes real commitment. DJ Moore finished with -0.1 points, a feat that deserves its own plaque, and Jordan Addison (4.1) and Jakobi Meyers (3.8) were no better. Brad named his team "Free Josh Jacobs" and then kept Jacobs on the bench for a 0.0, so nobody needs to free him from anything but Brad's lineup.

Brett beat Noah 125.88 to 93.20, and CeeDee Lamb (35.30) and DeVonta Smith (27.70) did so much of the work that Brett could have auto-drafted the rest of the lineup and still won. Brett still managed to start Colston Loveland for 1.30 points while Dalton Kincaid dropped 22.50 on his bench, and he rolled out the Lions D/ST for a gorgeous -4.00. Noah posted the lowest score of the week and did it with style, starting Puka Nacua for a flat zero while Jonah Coleman (14.80), Rachaad White (14.30) and Bhayshul Tuten (14.20) sat on the bench. His best players were a kicker (Harrison Butker, 16.00) and Jake Ferguson (20.30), and Justin Jefferson gave him 8.50 against an 18.36 projection. Brett wins by 32 points, but he should know the margin could have been about 55 if he'd read his own bench, and Noah should know a bench full of backs outscoring his starters is not a strategy.

Keith beat Brandon 163.56 to 119.16, and he should send Jaxon Smith-Njigba a fruit basket, because 42.5 points from a guy projected for 18.49 did most of the work. Keith's own lineup skills were on display too: Trevor Lawrence limped to 6.16 at QB, and George Kittle dropped 18.0 on the bench while Harold Fannin Jr. took the TE slot for 10.4. A 44-point win still can't hide that Keith got carried by one receiver and some rare good luck. Brandon's Bobby Light never stood a chance, with Javonte Williams producing 8.0 against a 16.7 projection and Travis Etienne Jr. posting 7.1 in the flex while Dontayvion Wicks sat on the bench with 12.4. Even Tre Tucker's 22.9 on a 9.86 projection couldn't save him, which says a lot about the rest of that roster.

Cody beat Tyler 132.28 to 96.12, and Brock Purdy did the heavy lifting with 28.48 points while Cody mostly stayed out of the way. Cody still managed to start Jadarian Price in a flex spot for 5.0 points while Denzel Boston sat on the bench with 20.5, and Josh Downs dropped 14.2 over there too, so he won by 36 despite his own lineup management. Saquon Barkley's 3.0 points against a 17.62 projection was also a real "thanks for coming" moment. Tyler's loss belongs to the passing game: Caleb Williams (7.72), Terry McLaurin (7.0), DK Metcalf (6.7) and Kyle Pitts Sr. (2.5) combined for 23.92 points, which is a bad weekend for one player, let alone four. Tyler also started Ashton Jeanty for 10.3 on a team literally named after him while Chuba Hubbard put up 14.4 on the bench, so the one thing Tyler committed to wasn't even right.

Reis dropped 141.26 on Kyle's 101.38, and a hefty chunk of that came from Bijan Robinson going off for 35.3 on a 19.54 projection, so congrats on riding one guy to a 40-point win. Reis still managed to bench Bo Nix's 24.14 for Josh Allen's 17.46, started a Patriots D/ST that scored a perfect zero, and slotted Jalen Coker into the flex for 3.8 points, which is a lot of self-inflicted damage in a blowout. Kyle, "WE GOT A SITUATION" is right, because that situation was Eagles D/ST putting up -1.0, Tetairoa McMillan managing 3.7 in the flex while Romeo Doubs sat on your bench with 7.9, and Amon-Ra St. Brown delivering 11.9 against a 19.86 projection. Malik Nabers (7.6), Breece Hall (8.5) and Mark Andrews (5.4) also turned up looking like they'd never met a fantasy scoreboard, so Kyle didn't lose to bad luck so much as to his own roster. Reis gets the W, but Kyle's team was so bad that Reis could win with that lineup and still leave about seven points on the bench.

Josh beat Noah 130.64 to 99.34, and the 31-point margin was far more comfortable than Josh's lineup management deserved. He sat Wan'Dale Robinson and his 18.7 points to start Jaylen Waddle's 6.4 in the flex, which cost him 12.3 points, and he still won by a mile. Noah, meanwhile, ran a three-man tire fire in Khalil Shakir (1.6), Terrance Ferguson (1.9) and a Bengals D/ST that scored a perfect zero, with Justin Jefferson's 5.2 in the flex slot as the cherry on top. Noah also benched Jake Ferguson's 9.3 and Rachaad White's 11.1 while those slots were producing next to nothing, so he spent Sunday proofreading his own bench instead of setting his lineup. Drake London dropped 28.4 and Lamar Jackson added 20.44, which makes it even sadder that Noah built a roster this good and still got run over by a Josh team starting Bryce Young.

Keith beat Brad 140.24 to 128.34, and he did it with Jaxon Smith-Njigba dropping 35.36 while Jonathan Taylor and Chase Brown combined for 18.1 points on two RB slots that wanted 37. Keith also left Harold Fannin Jr. and his 24.1 on the bench to start Dalton Schultz's 6.0, so this "win" came with the competence of a man who accidentally wandered into a trophy. Brad has no such excuse, because he benched Jordan Addison's 20.0 and Jakobi Meyers' 19.4 while Brian Thomas Jr. stunk up a starting spot with 1.8, and that one swap alone was worth more than the 11.9-point margin. Brad also started TreVeyon Henderson for 3.9 and kept Free Josh Jacobs on the bench, where he scored 0, which at least makes the team name the most accurate thing Brad has done all week. Brock Bowers went off for 27.6 and still couldn't save a lineup that Brad's own decisions had sabotaged.

Cody beat Brett 180.28 to 136.34, and the 43.94-point gap was about as competitive as a scrimmage against the practice squad. Jahmyr Gibbs dropped 41.4 (projected 25.35) and Brock Purdy added 31.28, so those two supplied 72.68 points while Cody mostly watched. Brett, meanwhile, started Dalton Kincaid for 3.8 points and left Kenyon Sadiq's 23.5 on the bench, then sat Aaron Jones (14.2) behind Quinshon Judkins (9.9), which suggests his lineup was set by throwing darts blindfolded. His kicker Will Reichard scored 16.0, out-producing Patrick Mahomes' 15.94, and a kicker beating your franchise QB is the most Spencer James Squad thing imaginable. Cody doesn't get off clean either: Saquon Barkley gave him 9.0 points, Jaylen Warren sat on the bench with 20.6, and the Steelers D/ST laid a 4.0 egg, so this was a win carried by two guys while the rest of the roster just collected checks.

Tyler beat Brandon 112.36 to 95.82, and Brandon has nobody to blame but himself, because Michael Wilson dropped 25.9 on his bench while Dontayvion Wicks sat in the lineup and laid a 5.2 egg. That one swap alone flips the result, and it's the kind of decision that should come with a mandatory apology to the group chat. Brandon also started De'Von Achane for 1.7 points against a 19.42 projection, a 49ers D/ST that scored 0, and a 4.0-point kicker, which is how you post the lowest score of the week. Tyler gets the win and zero style points, since he ran out Kyle Pitts for 1.5, Omarion Hampton for 5.6 and the Ravens D/ST for 1.0, then left Luther Burden III and Terry McLaurin sitting on the bench for nearly 40 combined points. Derrick Henry's 21.9 dragged Ashton 3:16 across the line, and Tyler wins this week mostly because Brandon's lineup was worse than his own.

Kyle beat Noah 180.72 to 120.78, a 59.94-point beatdown that Tetairoa McMillan basically ran solo with 45.20 from the flex spot, more than Noah got from Puka Nacua (27.7) and Drake London (14.6) combined. Kyle somehow made it harder than it needed to be, leaving Alvin Kamara (22.8) and Ollie Gordon II (18.0) on the bench while Jacory Croskey-Merritt gave him 7.0 and the Bills D/ST gave him a single point, so congrats on winning by 60 with a lineup that was actively trying to lose. Noah, meanwhile, got 4.3 from David Montgomery, 7.6 from Cam Skattebo (projected 16.12) and 6.0 from Harrison Butker, and still found time to bench Khalil Shakir's 13.2 and Keaton Mitchell's 11.3 for guys who scored 8.7 and 11.1. Lamar Jackson couldn't even hit his projection (18.88 vs. 21.2), so Noah didn't get much help from the guy he was counting on either. Kyle gets the W and a lecture on lineup setting, and Noah gets to explain why a team with that many underperformers is still called "Gno'msayin Mah-fkah."

Keith beat Reis 123.28 to 91.12, and he did it while parking Emanuel Wilson's 27.0 points on the bench and starting Parker Washington for a gorgeous 2.0. That's a 25-point self-inflicted wound, and he still won by 32, so the lineup was basically a Taylor Swift tribute act with D'Andre Swift chipping in 7.4 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba delivering 12.6 against a 21.86 projection. Keith's win owes plenty to Devaughn Vele going for 17.4 off the flex and Jonathan Taylor doing the heavy lifting, which is the kind of luck you don't get to call skill. Reis posted the lowest score of the week, getting 3.5 from Travis Kelce, 1.4 from Courtland Sutton and 5.7 from Garrett Wilson while Bijan Robinson's 27.7 was left to carry the whole team alone. Reis lost to a manager who forgot to start his best player, which is the kind of result that should come with a mandatory apology.

Cody beat Josh 164.32 to 118.16, but let's be honest: the win came from Nico Collins and Tee Higgins scoring 30.8 and 26.7 out of the flex spots, roughly double their projections, and not from any managerial genius. Gibbs gave Cody 17.7 against a 26.15 projection, Christian Watson stunk up a slot with 7.7, and the Steelers D/ST coughed up 5.0, so the 46-point margin is partly a gift. Josh deserves the real roasting, though, because Kyle Monangai (28.0) and Deebo Samuel Sr. (18.0) sat on his bench for 46.0 combined, almost exactly what he lost by. Meanwhile Ja'Marr Chase put up 5.7, Emeka Egbuka 3.3, and Jeremiyah Love 6.5, so Josh started three guys who couldn't beat his own bench. Bryce Young was Josh's best starter at 21.46, which tells you everything about how this lineup went.

Tyler beat Brad 186.28 to 127.90, a 58.38-point beating, and the week's highest score got there mostly because Kyren Williams dropped 36.7 on a 13.09 projection and Ka'imi Fairbairn, a kicker, chipped in 16. Tyler can call that a masterclass if he wants, but his Ashton 3:16 team name is still carried by someone who isn't Ashton Jeanty, and Caleb Williams and Terry McLaurin sat on his bench putting up zeroes like they were on a team-building retreat. Brad, meanwhile, left Brian Robinson Jr. and his 25.7 points on the bench while DJ Moore (2.7), TreVeyon Henderson (4.2) and the Texans D/ST (3.0) stank up the starting lineup, so he lost by 58 with a game-winning performance sitting right there in plain sight. The team is called "Free Josh Jacobs," and Jacobs scored 0 on Brad's bench, which feels like the most accurate thing Brad has ever done with a roster. Brad lost by a margin that suggests he wasn't just outplayed, he was out-managed, out-scouted and out-kicked, and the kicker he started scored 6.

Brett beat Brandon 131.40-116.72, and it was mostly CeeDee Lamb's 41.30 points doing the heavy lifting while Brett took the credit. Knock off Lamb's 24.4 points over projection and Brett loses this one 107.0 to 116.7, which is a lot of winning for a guy who started Ladd McConkey (0.0), Dalton Kincaid (1.7) and the Chiefs D/ST (1.0). Brett also left Quinshon Judkins (21.6) and Colston Loveland (11.7) on the bench, so he won while sitting a better lineup than the one he played. Brandon at least got 31.30 from Javonte Williams and 14.0 from Cam Little, then watched Rashee Rice lay a 0 on a 14.9 projection and Dontayvion Wicks add 4.8 while Tre Tucker sat on the bench with 8.4. Brandon, a Jalen Hurts that scored 13.52 is not a quarterback, it's a participation trophy.

Keith beat Kyle 147.04 to 140.10, and anyone who watched Parker Washington drop 30.4 on a 14.11 projection knows Keith got there by accident. Keith's own lineup did plenty to lose it, with Jonathan Taylor at 11.2, Chase Brown at 7.0 and George Kittle at 7.4, so a win built on a flex-level WR going nuclear isn't a strategy, it's a lottery ticket. Kyle gets to hate himself most, though, because Jacory Croskey-Merritt put up 14.2 on his bench while Alvin Kamara sat in the lineup and delivered 2.6, and that swap alone makes it 151.7 to 147.04 for the other side. Kyle also started Rome Odunze (5.0) and Mark Andrews (4.8), so he lost by 6.94 with a 14-point bench pile as the receipts. Keith should enjoy this one, since it was handed to him by Kyle's bad lineup decisions and not by anything he did.

Cody beat Noah 199.38 to 179.52 for the highest score of the week, and he did it while starting RJ Harvey (0.7 points) and the Steelers D/ST (1.0), so the rest of the league should be nervous about what happens when he finally sets a lineup right. Jahmyr Gibbs dropped 37.70, with Jaylen Warren (36.80), Isaiah Likely (32.40) and Christian Watson (32.30) all scoring more than double their projections, which makes this a win Cody mostly watched happen. He also left Denzel Boston's 13.60 on the bench while Harvey stunk up a flex spot, and Nico Collins and Chris Olave combined for 19.2 points as his WR1 and WR2, so the "genius" label stays in the drawer. Noah lost by nearly 20 despite a 37.70 from Puka Nacua, 27.32 from Matthew Stafford and a kicker (Spencer Shrader, 21.00) who outscored Justin Jefferson, which is a sentence nobody wants written about their season. Cam Skattebo (7.10) and Juwan Johnson (5.60) gave Noah almost nothing, Khalil Shakir sat on the bench with 11.00, and Lamar Jackson is still taking up a roster spot while scoring zero, so maybe the kicker should handle the lineup decisions too.

Reis dropped 156.90 on Tyler's 129.24, and it was less a victory than Bucky Irving (31.50 on a 15.24 projection) and Josh Allen (30.50) carrying a lineup that also started T.J. Hockenson for 1.70 points while Dallas Goedert sat on the bench with 9.80. Reis also left MarShawn Lloyd (16.70) and J.K. Dobbins (15.40) riding pine, so the winner basically beat Tyler with one hand and hid the other behind his own roster. Tyler, though, posted the lowest score of the week, and he earned it by starting Carnell Tate for 1.60 points while Terry McLaurin (12.20) and Woody Marks (12.50) watched from the bench. Omarion Hampton (4.90) and DK Metcalf (5.30) didn't help either, and Ashton Jeanty's 10.70 against a 17.84 projection was the cherry on top. Tyler needed his kicker (17.00 from Ka'imi Fairbairn) to be a top-tier offensive weapon just to lose by only 27.66, which is a damning review of everyone else he started.

Brandon edged Josh 136.88 to 135.26, a 1.62-point win that Josh handed over by starting Deebo Samuel Sr. (2.50) while Emeka Egbuka dropped 17.20 on his bench. Josh wasn't done, either: Jeremiyah Love gave him 2.20 in the RB slot while Blake Corum sat there with 16.20, so either swap alone wins this game, and doing both would have turned a heartbreaker into a blowout. Jayden Daniels went for 32.26 and Josh still lost, which takes real commitment to bad lineup management. Brandon, meanwhile, won by pure accident, riding the 49ers D/ST (20.00 against a 4.94 projection) and a 28-point George Pickens game that nobody on this planet saw coming. Michael Wilson (7.28) and Tony Pollard (5.20) were busy stinking up Brandon's lineup, so enjoy the W, champ, but a defense and a Pickens fluke did the work, not your genius.

Brett beat Brad 146.76 to 135.84, and Brad lost it with his own hands: Samaje Perine dropped 15.8 on his bench while TreVeyon Henderson sat in the lineup with 4.8, and that 11-point swap would have flipped the game by a whole 0.08. Brad also started DJ Moore for a big fat zero and left Josh Jacobs, the namesake of his own team, on the bench, so "Free Josh Jacobs" apparently meant "keep him locked up and out of my lineup." Brett wins, but he gets no medal for it, because Drake Maye's 39.46 did the heavy lifting while CeeDee Lamb (2.9), Colston Loveland (3.9) and Dalton Kincaid (3.7) lay around like they were on a team retreat. Brad's kicker (23.0) outscored Dak Prescott (12.64) and Christian McCaffrey (17.3), which tells you everything about this lineup and the man who built it. Brad lost by 10.92 points that he left on his own bench, and honestly, that's the most Brad way to go out.

roasts.1: Brett's C grade comes from a CeeDee Lamb first round followed by a pile of busts: Ladd McConkey is WR42 after going 31st overall, Marvin Harrison Jr. has 19.5 points, Rico Dowdle has 10.5, and Zach Charbonnet is still on the roster with a perfect zero.
roasts.2: Josh spent the No. 2 pick on Ja'Marr Chase, who is now WR10, and his best pick was a 16th-round Deebo Samuel, which tells you how well the first 15 rounds went.
roasts.3: Cody's A+ is padded by a pile of late-round steals, and it survives Saquon Barkley sitting at 23 points as RB42 with a second-round pick spent on him, plus Jadarian Price's 14 points, while he cut Matthew Stafford, who is QB4.
roasts.4: Brandon's F is earned: Rashee Rice (38.0), De'Von Achane (24.6) and Travis Etienne (30.9) went in his first three picks and have combined for 93.5 points, which Javonte Williams alone beat with 96.0 from round 9.
roasts.5: Tyler named his team Ashton 3:16 and then cut Ashton Jeanty, his own first-round pick, who is RB11 with 84.6 points, while Kyle Pitts sits at TE14 after being drafted as a TE3.
roasts.6: Keith's A- is the kind of grade you get when Jaxon Smith-Njigba is WR1 and everything else is a crime scene: A.J. Brown has 5.6 points, Jordyn Tyson has a flat zero, and Keith dropped both Jalen Coker (his best pick) and Will Reichard, the K1 with 68 points.
roasts.7: Brad named his team Free Josh Jacobs, but Jacobs is still on his roster with 0 points as RB49, so the only person holding him hostage is Brad, who also kept Tank Dell at a matching zero.
roasts.8: Noah gave up on Justin Jefferson, his No. 3 overall pick, and on Drake Maye, who is QB5 with 87.22 points, which is how you earn a B while dumping your two best stories.
roasts.9: Kyle's A- looks great until you remember he cut Romeo Doubs, his own best pick, and he's stuck with Breece Hall at RB29 and Jonathon Brooks at 9.3 points on his bench.
roasts.10: Reis has Josh Allen at QB1 with 142.96 points and still managed a B-, thanks to a Cowboys D/ST at negative one point, Isiah Pacheco at 0.0, and Courtland Sutton down at WR47.
